name: PPA-GF
bestUses: Insulating parts for machinery, electronics and automotive temperature exposure.

summary.text: PPA-GF is glass-fibre-filled polyphthalamide. Makers sell it for end-use automotive, aerospace and electronics parts. Semicrystalline, it carries light load well above its glass transition, and its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 152 °C. On the H2C every product needs a hardened nozzle, makers advise drying at 80⁠–⁠140 °C, 4⁠–⁠12 h, and some ask for more chamber heat than the H2C gives.

items.text: High rigidity/High strength/High-temperature resistance/Low creep

It is a modified polyphthalamide (PPA) containing 30% glass fiber, offering high-temperature resistance, high rigidity, and low shrinkage, with the ability to be printable on non-heated chamber FFF 3D printers.

Models printed with PPA-GF exhibit excellent tensile and impact strength, with a heat deflection temperature of up to 220°C. It also provides outstanding creep resistance at high temperatures, minimizing the impact of humidity and temperature on dimensional stability and electrical properties.

A high-temperature composite filament for end-use applications

The incorporation of short glass fibers (15wt.%) further improves upon the properties of PPA matrix, which makes PPA GF printed parts promising for end-use applications in automotive, aerospace, electrical and electronics (E&E) industry.

items.text: It's suitable for applications such as automotive parts, jigs & fixtures, as well as for insulating housings, etc.
Fiber-reinforced composite filaments are well known material for end-use parts production and heavy-duty applications with superior strength, stiff and heat resistance.
Hyper Core PPA GF25 is an ideal choice for diverse industrial applications where high performance, stability and cost-efficiency are required.
Jigs & Fixtures
Functional Parts
Manufacturing aids
Electrical and electronics (E&E) industry

To overcome these challenges, Raise3D has developed a new extrusion technology to form a cross-section of the filament with a fiber-rich inner core and a polymer-coated outer skin for the Hyper Core family.
The Hyper Core PPA GF25 is optimized for a fast melt rate in the hot end as well as a good balance of print efficiency, quality, performance and cost.

Thanks to the special coated skin and fiber (25wt.%) distribution structure, Hyper Core PPA GF25 exhibits a high stiffness (6.6 GPa), strength (98 MPa), heat resistance (189 ℃) as well as outstanding printing quality.
Tailored fiber distribution
High strength and stiffness
High temperature resistance
Cost-effectiveness
However, high-speed printing using fiber-reinforced filament brings many challenges, such as lower flowability and poorer interlayer bonding quality, and quicker wearing out of the nozzle.
After annealing, a maximum of 0.5% dimensional shrinkage may be observed along the Z-axis depending on infill and layer height, with no discernible dimensional shrinkage in XY-axis.
Smooth surface finish
As a result, Hyper Core PPA GF25 offers not only higher Z-direction strength, smoother surface quality, but also, and above all, higher performance-cost ratio and a wide range of color options.
During high-speed FFF printing, the thick polymer skin of Hyper Core PPA GF25 filament improves polymer healing and welding process across the interface of adjacent layers and lines.
Enhanced interlayer bonding
After drying, we recommend storing the filament into Raise3D Filament Dry Box during the printing.

items.agent: Bio-diesel fuel, brake fluid, synthetic motor oil, transmission fluid, glycols
items.text: Amodel PPA's highly aromatic ring structure provides greater resistance to a broader range of chemicals than standard, linear aliphatic nylons, even at high temperatures. This enables automotive, electrical and industrial components to withstand prolonged exposure to harsh chemicals: bio-diesel fuel, brake fluid, calcium chloride, glycols, synthetic motor oil, road salt, transmission fluid, zinc chloride.
items.conditions: Prolonged exposure
